text:
jess: Heads-up: after the prefetch scheduler tweak landed in canary the last two deploys, we're seeing a p95 latency bump on steady-state traffic and a ~7% drop in prefix cache hit-rate. Not huge but reproducible in staging. Anyone else seeing this?

omar: I noticed similar in the perf dashboard. The change that went in moves from fixed-window prefetch to aggressive continuous prefetch when batch sizes go above 8. The idea was to warm more KVs earlier, but looks like it causes batch composition to favor shorter prefixes and thrashes eviction.

liam: Can you paste the exact change? I only looked at the PR title.

jess: Here's the relevant config we rolled:

```json
{"prefetch": {"mode": "continuous", "threshold": 8, "lookahead_tokens": 64, "stagger_ms": 0}}
```

jess: Before it was `mode: burst` with `stagger_ms: 5` and `lookahead_tokens: 32`.

omar: Profiling notes: when continuous mode is on, we see the request queue coalesce into many small microbatches dominated by warmup-only requests. Those requests allocate KV slots, then larger user requests arrive and evict the warmed entries because the scheduler packs by arrival time not prefix fingerprint. Hit-rate drops.

rachel: That matches an experiment I ran locally: sample workload with 70% short prefix churn and 30% sticky prefixes. Continuous prefetch increased warmup ops by ~40% and forced more evictions on sticky prefixes -> higher p95.

liam: Do we have the batch composition histograms? I want to see distribution of prefix-length vs batch size vs KV occupancy.

omar: Quick dump from staging (trimmed):

```
batch_size_histogram: {1: 4200, 2: 1800, 4: 900, 8: 200, 16: 40}
pref_warm_ops: 12.3 ops/s/node
kv_evictions_per_min: 18 -> 35 (post-change)
cache_hit_rate_over_time: 0.82 -> 0.75
p95_latency_ms: 112 -> 140
```

jess: Notable: batch_size shifted towards smaller batches due to the prefetch tasks being enqueued as separate lightweight requests. We used to coalesce them.

rachel: Hypothesis: continuous prefetch increases queue churn which reduces effective coalescing window. Two knobs to test: re-introduce a small stagger (1-3ms) and change coalescer to group by prefix fingerprint before batch formation.

liam: Grouping by prefix fingerprint sounds promising but might hurt fairness for bursty single users. Could add a size floor: only fingerprint-group when group size >= 3, else fall back to arrival order.

omar: Another option: mark prefetch requests as "low priority" and place them behind user inference requests in queueing, but still allow limited in-flight prefetch per worker slot. That prevents prefetch from evicting sticky KVs.

jess: Agreed. Also we should clearly separate KV reservation from token-level batching. Right now prefetch allocates full KV slots immediately. We could do a lightweight reservation and fully materialize only when batch forms.

rachel: I ran a small sim: apply a 2ms stagger + low-priority prefetch + fingerprint-grouping threshold 3 -> simulated hit-rate recovers to 0.81 and p95 back to ~116ms. Not perfect but much closer.

liam: Nice. Can you add those three knobs into a canary config set? Maybe call it `prefetch-friendly` and run against the churny workload.

jess: I'll push a canary with this config:

```yaml
prefetch:
  mode: continuous
  threshold: 8
  lookahead_tokens: 48
  stagger_ms: 2
  priority: low
coalescer:
  fingerprint_group_threshold: 3
  max_group_delay_ms: 4
kv:
  reservation_mode: "soft"
```

infra-bot: Deploy queued: canary/prefetch-friendly -> env=staging, id=canary-2026-03-18-08

omar: Once canary is up, collect: batch_size_hist, kv_evictions, cache_hit_rate_by_prefix_cohort, p50/p95. Also enable tracing for one hotspot worker to see prefetch and user requests interleaving.

jess: Will do. If this reproduces improvement we can consider a rollout with a toggle that sets prefetch priority per-customer (dedicated vs hosted).

liam: One more thing — check kernel selection costs during this churn. If continuous prefetch creates many tiny batches, we may be choosing fast but suboptimal kernels more often (kernel-switch overhead). That could also add to p95.

rachel: Good call. I saw kernel_switch_count spike slightly in the profiling dump. Add that to the canary metrics.

jess: Plan summary: 1) run canary `prefetch-friendly` 2) collect histograms + kernel switch counts + per-prefix hit-rate 3) tweak thresholds if needed 4) if stable, roll to low-traffic nodes first.

omar: I'll prepare the dashboards and a small eval harness that can replay churny traces.

jess: Thanks. If we see any regression after canary I'll roll back immediately. :thumbsup:

rachel: FYI I'll also try an alternate approach: keep continuous prefetch but limit total prefetch inflight per worker to X (experiment with 2/4). That might be simpler than priority buckets.

jess: Great. Keep notes in the perf-run thread. We'll sync tomorrow in standup if canary completes.

infra-bot: Canary deployed successfully (canary-2026-03-18-08)
